overview: The most significant submission of the day was Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi's RFC series introducing unwinding support for synchronous BPF callbacks, which would allow callbacks to longjmp past their helper call frame back to the original caller. Alongside this, a new bpf_path_getattr() helper was proposed for reading filesystem path attributes from BPF programs, and fixes landed for task work use-after-free and suspicious RCU usage in sleepable programs.

patches.title: bpf: Give a helper a way to call its callback with a pad
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: This RFC series (11 patches) introduces a mechanism for BPF callbacks to unwind past their helper's call frame. The core idea is to give helper calls a reserved 'pad' slot in the JIT-emitted code so a callback can longjmp back to the caller's execution context. The series extends the arm64 JIT, the verifier, and several helpers (bpf_loop, bpf_for_each_map_elem, bpf_find_vma, bpf_user_ringbuf_drain, bpf_rbtree_add) to permit unwinding. This is a long-requested capability that enables early-exit patterns in BPF callback-driven loops without requiring a dedicated helper for each use case.

patches.title: bpf: Add bpf_path_getattr()
patches.author: Anastasios Papagiannis
patches.summary: This 3-patch series adds a new BPF helper bpf_path_getattr() that allows BPF programs to retrieve filesystem attributes (such as device, inode, mode, and size) for a given path. The implementation uses an existing kernel struct path pointer obtained from BPF context, providing a safe way for security and observability programs to inspect file metadata without leaving the BPF sandbox. Documentation and selftests are included.

patches.title: bpf: Retire task work before reclaiming hash elements
patches.author: Yun Lu
patches.summary: This 2-patch series fixes a use-after-free bug in BPF hash map element reclamation when task work is in flight. When a hash map element is deleted while a task work referencing it is pending, the memory can be freed before the work runs. The fix ensures pending task work is retired before the element's memory is reclaimed, and a selftest exercises the concurrent deletion path.

patches.title: bpf: Fix suspicious RCU usage for sleepable bpf_get_stack()
patches.author: Feng Yang
patches.summary: This single-patch fix addresses incorrect RCU usage in the bpf_get_stack() helper when called from a sleepable BPF program. Sleepable programs execute in a context where standard rcu_read_lock() is insufficient; the patch switches to the appropriate RCU API for sleepable contexts to eliminate the kernel warning and prevent potential memory safety issues.

patches.title: bpftool: Fix disposal of the LLVM disassembler context
patches.author: Mark Korenberg
patches.summary: This 2-patch v3 series improves bpftool's LLVM disassembler integration. The first patch fixes a resource leak by properly disposing of the LLVM disassembler context on cleanup. The second patch makes the LLVM disassembler an optional runtime dependency via dlopen(), so bpftool can fall back gracefully when LLVM libraries are not installed rather than failing to start. This improves portability and packaging flexibility.

patches.title: selftests/bpf: Build callx tests with GCC that defines __BPF_FEATURE_CALLX
patches.author: Vineet Gupta
patches.summary: This v2 8-patch series cleans up the BPF selftests build system for GCC compatibility. Key changes include not passing clang-only warning flags to GCC, properly reporting SKIP for arena tests that GCC cannot build, suppressing spurious -Warray-bounds warnings in arena_base(), and rewriting mixed arena/scalar ALU tests in assembly so both compilers can handle them. The series also ensures struct_ops arena tests are skipped without compiler support and fixes test result reporting to avoid false positives.

patches.title: selftests/bpf: libarena: Order equal rbtree keys FIFO
patches.author: Changwoo Min
patches.summary: This 3-patch series enhances the arena-based rbtree library used in BPF selftests with two new capabilities. The first patch makes the ordering of equal keys stable (FIFO) to improve test determinism. The second caches the leftmost node and total count to make O(1) minimum-key lookup and size queries available. The third adds an rb_next() iterator for ordered in-order traversal, enabling lockless peek semantics for test programs that inspect the tree.
